sources.entry: anyio - A high-level async concurrency and networking framework that works on top of asyncio or trio.

summary.one_liner: AnyIO is an async networking and concurrency library that runs unmodified on either asyncio or Trio.
summary.what_it_does: AnyIO provides Trio-style structured concurrency (task groups) on top of asyncio, and works alongside Trio's native structured concurrency when run on Trio. It offers high-level TCP, UDP and UNIX socket networking, including a happy eyeballs algorithm for TCP connections and async/await UDP sockets. It includes byte and object streams, inter-task synchronization primitives (locks, conditions, events, semaphores, futures), worker threads, subprocesses, and asynchronous file I/O. It also covers signal handling, asynchronous versions of functools and itertools, and a pytest plugin with async fixture support that works with Hypothesis. The README states that code written against AnyIO's API can be adopted incrementally into an existing project.
use_cases: write async code that runs on both asyncio and Trio
add structured concurrency to an asyncio project
high-level TCP, UDP or UNIX socket networking
run blocking code in worker threads from async code
testing async code with pytest and Hypothesis
notable: Runs unmodified on either asyncio or Trio backends
Trio-like task groups (structured concurrency) on asyncio
Async UDP sockets without transports and protocols
Subinterpreter support on Python 3.13 and later
caveats: Subinterpreter support requires Python 3.13 or later
README gives no installation commands in the text provided
keywords: run code on asyncio or trio
